what: Classify Match Decision and Review Requirement — classify_match_decision
title: Classify Match Decision and Review Requirement — classify_match_decision
text: Determines whether candidate match automatically accepted flagged manual review, based strength uniqueness match. function operates top-ranked matches produced matching pipeline applies set heuristic rules using exact, partial, fuzzy matching signals.

title: Classify Match Decision and Review Requirement — classify_match_decision
code: classify_match_decision(   best_matches,   all_partial,   strong_fuzzy_threshold = 0.92,   min_auto_confidence = 0.75 )

title: Classify Match Decision and Review Requirement — classify_match_decision
text: best_matches Data frame best candidate matches (typically subset matches highest confidence score). all_partial Full data frame candidate matches prior filtering, used context (e.g. identifying ambiguity). strong_fuzzy_threshold Numeric. Threshold fuzzy similarity considered strong (default 0.92). min_auto_confidence Numeric. Minimum confidence required allow automatic acceptance match (default 0.75).

title: Classify Match Decision and Review Requirement — classify_match_decision
text: list components: match_method Character string describing match found       (e.g. "EXACT", "PARTIAL START", "FUZZY"). match_decision Character string describing whether match       automatically accepted requires review. review_required Logical; TRUE match       manually reviewed, FALSE otherwise.

title: Classify Match Decision and Review Requirement — classify_match_decision
text: function distinguishes : Match method: match identified (e.g. exact,     token match, fuzzy). Match decision: whether match can automatically     accepted reviewed. Review flag: logical indicator whether manual review     required. Typical behaviour: Exact full matches automatically accepted. Matches exact surnames single strong first-name match     (exact, token, partial start, high fuzzy) automatically accepted. Matches involving swapped names, multiple equally strong candidates,     non-exact surnames, weak fuzzy similarity flagged review.

title: Classify Match Decision and Review Requirement — classify_match_decision
code: # Example using mock matching output df = data.frame(   FN_exact = c(TRUE),   LN_exact = c(TRUE),   FN_exact_token = c(TRUE),   LN_exact_token = c(TRUE),   FN_partial_start = c(TRUE),   LN_partial_start = c(TRUE),   FN_fuzzy = c(1),   LN_fuzzy = c(1),   match_confidence = c(1),   match_method = c("EXACT"),   match_orientation = c("STANDARD"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  classify_match_decision(   best_matches = df,   all_partial = df ) #> $match_method #> [1] "EXACT" #>  #> $match_decision #> [1] "AUTO: exact full match" #>  #> $review_required #> [1] FALSE #>

title: Clean and Standardise School Names for Matching — clean_school_name
text: function performs following steps: Converts text lowercase Transliterates ASCII (e.g. removes accents) Removes punctuation Normalises whitespace (collapses multiple spaces) Applies common domain-specific replacements (e.g. "math" → "mathematics") Optionally removes whitespace function designed use school name matching workflows, ensuring equivalent names minor formatting differences likely match.

text: Computes similarity score two names using token-level Jaro-Winkler similarity. Names first standardised upper case, punctuation removed, strings split tokens. similarity matrix formed tokens name, token longer name best match shorter name taken. final score mean best matches.

title: Compute Token-Based Jaro-Winkler Name Similarity — name_similarity_jw
code: name_similarity_jw(x, y)

title: Compute Token-Based Jaro-Winkler Name Similarity — name_similarity_jw
text: x Character string. First name string compare. y Character string. Second name string compare.

title: Compute Token-Based Jaro-Winkler Name Similarity — name_similarity_jw
text: Numeric scalar 0 1, NA_real_   either name valid tokens cleaning.

title: Compute Token-Based Jaro-Winkler Name Similarity — name_similarity_jw
text: returns value 0 1, : 1 indicates exact token-level match values closer 0 indicate weaker similarity

title: Compute Token-Based Jaro-Winkler Name Similarity — name_similarity_jw
code: name_similarity_jw("Matthew", "Matt") #> [1] 0.8571429 name_similarity_jw("Janet Brown", "Janet Browne") #> [1] 0.9722222

what: Compute Partial and Fuzzy Matching Signals for a Single Name — partial_fuzzy_match
title: Compute Partial and Fuzzy Matching Signals for a Single Name — partial_fuzzy_match
text: Compares single input name vector candidate names returns several matching signals. include exact string match, token overlap, prefix matching, substring matching, initial matching, token-based Jaro-Winkler fuzzy similarity.

title: Compute Partial and Fuzzy Matching Signals for a Single Name — partial_fuzzy_match
code: partial_fuzzy_match(name, all_names, do_clean_name = FALSE)

title: Compute Partial and Fuzzy Matching Signals for a Single Name — partial_fuzzy_match
text: name Character scalar. single name match. all_names Character vector candidate names compare . do_clean_name Logical; TRUE, applies clean_name() name all_names matching.

title: Compute Partial and Fuzzy Matching Signals for a Single Name — partial_fuzzy_match
text: data frame one row per element all_names   following columns: given_name input name. data_name candidate name all_names. exact Logical; exact full-string match. exact_token Logical; least one token matches exactly. partial_start Logical; least one token matches start       token either direction. partial_anywhere Logical; least one token matches anywhere       within token either direction. initial_token Logical; least one token shares initial. fuzzy Numeric token-based Jaro-Winkler similarity       0 1.

title: Compute Partial and Fuzzy Matching Signals for a Single Name — partial_fuzzy_match
text: function designed support downstream person linkage workflows first last names scored separately combined.

title: Compute Partial and Fuzzy Matching Signals for a Single Name — partial_fuzzy_match
code: all_names = c("MATTHEW", "MATT", "MARK", "JANET") partial_fuzzy_match("Matt", all_names) #>         given_name data_name exact exact_token partial_start partial_anywhere #> MATTHEW       Matt   MATTHEW FALSE       FALSE          TRUE             TRUE #> MATT          Matt      MATT FALSE       FALSE          TRUE             TRUE #> MARK          Matt      MARK FALSE       FALSE         FALSE            FALSE #> JANET         Matt     JANET FALSE       FALSE         FALSE            FALSE #>         initial_token     fuzzy #> MATTHEW          TRUE 0.8571429 #> MATT             TRUE 1.0000000 #> MARK             TRUE 0.6666667 #> JANET           FALSE 0.6333333

code: people = data.frame(   FN = c("MATTHEW", "MATT", "MARK"),   LN = c("JONES", "JONES", "JONES"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  x = matching_breakdown("Matt", "Jones", people, "FN", "LN") rank_name_matches(x) #>        FN    LN FN_given_name FN_data_name FN_exact FN_exact_token #> 1    MATT JONES          Matt         MATT    FALSE          FALSE #> 2 MATTHEW JONES          Matt      MATTHEW    FALSE          FALSE #> 3    MARK JONES          Matt         MARK    FALSE          FALSE #>   FN_partial_start FN_partial_anywhere FN_initial_token  FN_fuzzy LN_given_name #> 1             TRUE                TRUE             TRUE 1.0000000         Jones #> 2             TRUE                TRUE             TRUE 0.8571429         Jones #> 3            FALSE               FALSE             TRUE 0.6666667         Jones #>   LN_data_name LN_exact LN_exact_token LN_partial_start LN_partial_anywhere #> 1        JONES    FALSE          FALSE             TRUE                TRUE #> 2        JONES    FALSE          FALSE             TRUE                TRUE #> 3        JONES    FALSE          FALSE             TRUE                TRUE #>   LN_initial_token LN_fuzzy mean_fuzzy match_score match_confidence #> 1             TRUE        1  1.0000000    6.500000        0.4482759 #> 2             TRUE        1  0.9285714    6.285714        0.4334975 #> 3             TRUE        1  0.8333333    3.000000        0.2068966 #>    match_method #> 1 PARTIAL START #> 2 PARTIAL START #> 3 PARTIAL/FUZZY

what: Score Combined First-Name and Last-Name Matches — score_name_matches
title: Score Combined First-Name and Last-Name Matches — score_name_matches
text: Combines separate first-name last-name matching signals single composite score scaled confidence measure 0 1.

title: Score Combined First-Name and Last-Name Matches — score_name_matches
code: score_name_matches(   partial_matching,   w_exact_both = 5,   w_exact_token_both = 3,   w_partial_start_both = 2,   w_partial_anywhere_both = 1,   w_initial_both = 0.5,   w_fuzzy_mean = 3 )

title: Score Combined First-Name and Last-Name Matches — score_name_matches
text: partial_matching Data frame returned matching_breakdown(). w_exact_both Numeric weight applied first last names exactly match. w_exact_token_both Numeric weight applied first last names exact token matches. w_partial_start_both Numeric weight applied first last names partially match start token. w_partial_anywhere_both Numeric weight applied first last names partially match anywhere within token. w_initial_both Numeric weight applied first last names share token initials. w_fuzzy_mean Numeric weight applied mean first-name last-name fuzzy similarity.

title: Score Combined First-Name and Last-Name Matches — score_name_matches
text: input data frame additional columns: mean_fuzzy Mean FN_fuzzy LN_fuzzy. match_score Composite matching score. match_confidence Scaled confidence 0       1.

title: Score Combined First-Name and Last-Name Matches — score_name_matches
text: score heuristic rather probabilistic. intended rank candidate matches provide interpretable confidence-like measure.

code: people = data.frame(   FN = c("MATTHEW", "MATT"),   LN = c("JONES", "JONES"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  x = matching_breakdown("Matt", "Jones", people, "FN", "LN") score_name_matches(x) #>              FN    LN FN_given_name FN_data_name FN_exact FN_exact_token #> MATTHEW MATTHEW JONES          Matt      MATTHEW    FALSE          FALSE #> MATT       MATT JONES          Matt         MATT    FALSE          FALSE #>         FN_partial_start FN_partial_anywhere FN_initial_token  FN_fuzzy #> MATTHEW             TRUE                TRUE             TRUE 0.8571429 #> MATT                TRUE                TRUE             TRUE 1.0000000 #>         LN_given_name LN_data_name LN_exact LN_exact_token LN_partial_start #> MATTHEW         Jones        JONES    FALSE          FALSE             TRUE #> MATT            Jones        JONES    FALSE          FALSE             TRUE #>         LN_partial_anywhere LN_initial_token LN_fuzzy mean_fuzzy match_score #> MATTHEW                TRUE             TRUE        1  0.9285714    6.285714 #> MATT                   TRUE             TRUE        1  1.0000000    6.500000 #>         match_confidence #> MATTHEW        0.4334975 #> MATT           0.4482759
